start.title: The River Sings
start.text: The frozen river ahead hums with long, whale-like notes as the current shifts beneath the ice. The normal crossing has drifted over, leaving no visible markers.

choices.text: Use the sound to judge the ice

buckets.flavourText: The deepest tones come from thick, stressed plates; the high ticking marks the dangerous seams. You plot a crooked but safe line.
You identify the worst areas, but one broad shelf still gives uncertain notes.
The river is all echoes. Every patch sounds dangerous once you listen too long.

safe_cross.title: A Crooked Path
safe_cross.text: You cross in a series of careful angles. The ice complains but does not shift. Halfway over, you find an old pole frozen upright—the remains of last winter's marker.

uncertain_cross.title: The Broad Shelf
uncertain_cross.text: The only reasonable route crosses a pale shelf where trapped bubbles run like strings of beads beneath your boots.

buckets.flavourText: The shelf flexes once and holds. You do not stop until both boots reach snow again.
A crack shoots between your feet and the shelf drops several inches.

choices.text: Backtrack and take the long way

through.title: One Leg Through
through.text: Your left leg punches through to the thigh. The current is shallow here, but the cold clamps around the muscle immediately.

choices.text: Get out before the hole widens

buckets.flavourText: You throw your weight flat and drag the leg free.
The first pull breaks more ice. You have to crawl backward on your elbows before the leg comes loose.

cold_exit.title: A Wet Walk Home
cold_exit.text: You reach the bank with one trouser leg already stiffening. The river keeps singing behind you as if nothing happened.

long_way.title: The Long Bank
long_way.text: You follow the river until the banks narrow around a timber footbridge. It costs time, but the planks do not sing beneath your feet.
